narrative.overview: MYPOS builds and sells the physical POS terminals, self-order kiosks, and weigh-and-pay stations that Thai shops run every night after the lights go down and the till is still glowing. The visual system takes that literally: a near-black interface that reads like a terminal screen left on after close, with the brand's ember orange doing the work a receipt printer's LED or an active register display would. This is a manufacturer's site, not a reseller's storefront: every visual choice should read as 'we built this and stand behind it.'
keyCharacteristics: Near-black base surfaces with layered depth (four surface steps, not one flat panel)
Ember orange used deliberately — gradient fills and glow accents, never wallpaper
Motion is ambient and slow — never bouncy or attention-grabbing for its own sake
Every decorative element must be grounded in something real — no floating icon-soup badges with no label

rules.name: The One Register Rule
rules.body: Ember orange is the only color allowed on a primary call-to-action. Interface Blue, success green, and warning amber are supporting cast.

rules.name: The No-Monospace-For-Language Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for genuinely monospaced content only. Default every UI label to Prompt — Thai/Chinese metrics clip in monospace fonts.

rules.name: The Glow-On-Response Rule
rules.body: Ambient orange glow only appears on the primary CTA at rest and on any card the instant it's hovered/focused. It never sits on static, non-interactive content.

dos: Do use Ember Orange (#e85520) as the only color on primary CTAs.
Do ground every decorative or motion element in something real — an actual customer photo and logo, an actual number, an actual product photo.
Do set eyebrow/label text in the Prompt sans stack, never JetBrains Mono.
Do group navigation by what the visitor is trying to do, folding low-traffic pages into a shared 'Resources' menu.
Do use the orange glow only on interactive elements at rest or on hover.
donts: Don't ship a floating decorative badge (icon + pattern, no text) with a bob/float animation.
Don't design this as a boring corporate/factory site — no navy-and-gray B2B palette, no stock handshake photography, no dense text walls.
Don't tip into discount-marketplace energy — no red sale badges, no countdown timers, no Shopee/Lazada-style promotional grids.
Don't apply monospace fonts to any UI label, eyebrow, or Thai/Chinese body text.
Don't let the top nav sprawl past roughly 4-5 top-level items.
